name: Drive safely on snow and ice
blurb: Smoothness and space, not skill at the limit. Most winter accidents come from doing something abruptly, and the fixes are simple once you know them.
gear: Winter or all-season tyres, which matter more than drive type
An empty snow-covered car park to practise in
A winter kit in the boot
steps: Clear the whole car before moving: all windows, lights, roof and number plate.
Do everything gently — accelerate, brake and steer as if there is an open cup of coffee on the dash.
Increase your following distance to at least four times the usual, and brake far earlier than feels necessary.
Practise emergency braking in a safe empty space to feel ABS pulsing, so you do not lift off when it happens for real.
Learn skid recovery: look and steer where you want to go, ease off the accelerator, do not stamp on the brake.
Learn to pull away in a higher gear on slick surfaces to reduce wheelspin.
tips: Four-wheel drive helps you go, not stop. It gives false confidence on ice.
Black ice appears on bridges and shaded spots first. Treat those as ice even when the road looks clear.
proof: You handle a snowy journey calmly, with correct following distances and no abrupt inputs.
